shapes.name: array_length
shapes.reason: An array's own length, not a caller-supplied number. A JS array cannot be longer than the safe-integer range, so the read has nothing to saturate; the budget on that length is the array-length guard's, which the shared wasmArrayLikeLength applies.

shapes.name: array_element
shapes.reason: An element read from an array whose length was taken first, indexed by the loop counter. The value is a caller-supplied number like any other, but the receiver is the element rather than a named option, so it carries no field name a range error could report; the element's own domain is checked where the struct it fills is validated.

narrowings.reason: An enum ordinal range-checked against the warp-mode bounds before the cast is used, so a saturated value is refused by name.

readers.reason: Not a conversion: the narrowing is delegated whole to the shared intProperty, and what is local is the field's own domain. The shared reader guarantees the value survived the conversion unchanged, which a negative frame count does, and nothing downstream asks whether one means anything -- the peak picker returned an ordinary onset list for -1. The six onset window fields are the only place that domain applies, so asking it at the field keeps it off every other integer option.

A default seeder rather than an options-bag reader: it rejects a non-number, turns a non-positive value into a deterministic seed, and refuses anything past the type's maximum by name. Every value in the type's range is a legal seed, so truncating a fractional one cannot land outside the domain -- driving it, a seed moves the synthesized response, 4294967296 and Infinity are refused, and 0 / -1 / NaN all fall back to the documented default.

Delegates its narrowing to the shared checkedFloatFromVal rather than casting, so the conversion contract is single-sourced and only the default-and-absence handling is local. Kept out of the shared header for the same reason as its integer sibling: its options bag is positional in a way the generic reader is not. Not the same defect as the integer one and it had to be measured separately -- an overflow here produces inf rather than a plausible in-domain number, and the config validator refuses NaN but accepted inf, so four distinct absurd requests reached one identical result.

Delegates its narrowing to the shared checkedIntFromVal rather than casting, so the conversion contract is single-sourced and only the default-and-absence handling is local. Kept out of the shared header because its options bag is positional in a way the generic reader is not.

An enum resolver for the pan-law ordinal, taking the string and numeric spellings together. The numeric path requires a finite, integral value inside the enum's bounds before the cast, so a saturated, negative, fractional or non-finite ordinal is refused by name; the two legal ordinals pan differently, which is what makes those refusals a measurement rather than an unread field.

Reads through double rather than narrowing, so no integer cast happens here and the inline-narrowing population does not see it. It is a second numeric reader outside the shared family all the same. Its own range check is the mechanism: a value outside [0, max] or a fractional one is refused naming the field, and a non-finite one is refused by the shared requireNumberProperty it reads through.

The floating-point sibling of integerField, under the same standing. It type-checks and refuses a non-finite value through the shared requireNumberProperty and returns the double unnarrowed; the float narrowing is the caller's, and it can only overflow for values already far outside the field's physical domain, where the representable neighbours render identically.

An enum resolver for the sample loop mode, accepting the SoundFont numeric value and the name spellings. The numeric path is integerField's, so the ordinal is refused outside [0, 3] and for a fractional or non-finite value; an unknown name is refused naming the accepted set.

An enum resolver, not a size reader: the ordinal it returns is range-checked by the C ABI against the curve enum's bounds. Recorded here rather than folded into the shared family because the reader shape is incidental -- it exists to accept both the string and the numeric spelling of one enum.

The sibling enum resolver for the automation target kind. Like automationCurveFromVal it exists to accept both spellings of one enum, and its numeric path requires a finite, integral ordinal inside the enum's bounds before the cast, so a saturated, negative or fractional one is refused rather than landing on a member.

shapes.name: sixty_four_bit

mechanism.note: The shipped embind glue, where the 64-bit toWireType lives. It is the build's output and no committed file carries it, so the citation is marked built: an absent dist is not a failure, a dist whose glue no longer reads this way is. The other half of the claim -- that this population is the 64-bit one at all -- is derived from the declared types rather than cited.

shapes.reason: A 64-bit parameter is registered through __embind_register_bigint, not through the integer path: its toWireType converts a JS number with BigInt(value), which throws on a fractional and on a non-finite one, and no number below 2^63 has anything to wrap into. The blessing belongs to the width, not to the field: this pattern selects on the declared type alone, so the population is every 64-bit parameter -- timeline positions and page ordinals alike -- and naming it after one of those meanings would claim a check nothing performs. The one residue is a request past 2^63, where the BigInt-to-i64 conversion truncates; it is integral, so it cannot arrive by the fractional truncation these records exist for, and no field of any meaning here addresses a domain that large.

shapes.name: entity_handle
shapes.selects: an existing track, clip, bus, marker, take, page provider or automation parameter
shapes.reason: A handle resolved against a live registry. A request of 2^32 + n arrives as n and addresses the entity whose id is n, and the guards in front of these are `id == 0` tests, which refuse only the exact multiple of 2^32. Measured on the one this class is named after: midiParamToCc matched the binding whose id is 5 for a requested 4294967301, which is why its paramId is now read as a val through checkedUintFromVal while its siblings are not.

shapes.name: slot_index
shapes.selects: a real strip, insert, send, lane, band or candidate slot
shapes.reason: An ordinal into a container whose bounds are checked after the conversion, so the check sees the wrapped value and not the requested one. setLaneSidechain and setTrackStripInsertBypassed take their insertIndex this way: the engine refuses an index past the end, which a wrapped one is not.

shapes.name: midi_selector
shapes.selects: a real MIDI group, channel, note, program or controller
shapes.reason: A 4-bit or 7-bit selector guarded by an explicit range test -- pushMidiInputCc requires group and channel in [0,15] and controller and value in [0,127] -- and the test runs on the wrapped value. 2^32 + 3 arrives as 3, passes, and sends on channel 3. The object-field spelling of the same defect is already fixed: channel 511 used to arrive as 255, the any-channel wildcard.

shapes.name: enumerated_mode
shapes.selects: a named member of a small enum -- a pan law, a warp mode, an automation curve, a key
shapes.reason: An ordinal whose whole domain is a handful of adjacent values, so a wrapped request lands on a member rather than outside the enum. The bounds check that would refuse an absurd ordinal is downstream of the conversion and never sees one.

shapes.name: extent_or_size
shapes.selects: a different analysis: another sample rate, FFT size, hop, frame count or matrix shape
shapes.reason: The residue, graded as a family rather than per site, and graded open because open is the answer that does not bless anything: putting a site here claims only that nobody has shown a mechanism. Two members were measured. sample_rate is bounded to [kMinAudioSampleRate, kMaxAudioSampleRate] by validate_offline_audio_extent, so 2^32 + 44100 is accepted and analyses at 44100. The matrix extents looked like the exception -- load_segment_matrix requires length == rows * cols -- and are not: a buffer has several factorisations, so a wrapped rows can land on a different valid reading of the same data.

constructors.selects: a different stream-analysis configuration: sample rate, FFT size, hop
constructors.reason: The StreamAnalyzer constructor spells its parameter types in the registration, so nothing points at a declaration and the arity is the key. Same shape as extent_or_size, recorded separately because the scan reaches it by a different route.

constructors.selects: a different block size or ring capacity for the engine being constructed
constructors.reason: The four-argument RealtimeEngine constructor. maxBlockSize and the two ring capacities wrap, and the capacity ceiling is applied after the conversion.

constructors.selects: a different block size, ring capacity or channel count
constructors.reason: The five-argument overload of the same constructor, which adds maxChannels. Recorded apart from the four-argument one because two overloads in one file are told apart only by how many arguments they take.
